risks.text: Share count and net debt are both unsourced estimates, and together they determine every per-share valuation figure here.
Roughly USD 30bn of net debt against volatile merchant earnings is materially less resilient than a contracted-infrastructure framing implies.

Completion of the Brazos Valley sale

conclusions: This is the weakest evidence base in the series. Shares outstanding and net debt are both estimates, and they are precisely the inputs that convert enterprise value into per-share value.

The one reliable anchor is the earnings multiple: at USD 283.78 against a guidance midpoint of USD 12.00, the stock trades at approximately 23.6x FY2026 adjusted operating earnings, and that figure does not depend on the share count.

Leverage is the real balance-sheet story. Roughly USD 30bn of estimated net debt against volatile merchant earnings is a different risk profile from the contracted-infrastructure framing in the thesis.
Nuclear sustaining capital — refuelling, licence renewal, life extension — is permanent, large and unquantified. It is the gap between this fleet's EBITDA and its free cash flow.
Return on capital cannot be assessed: the acquisition closed within the year and the capital base has been transformed.
thesisImpact: Phase 4 requires the valuation in Phase 5 to be presented with an explicit confidence caveat, and gives disproportionate weight to the one multiple that does not depend on estimated inputs.
